It's the same with this Youtube thing. For the overwhelming majority of users, if they're experiencing artifacting, downscaled resolutions or other viewing issues with 1080p videos its because of an issue somewhere between their device and Youtube, not with Youtube itself. TB's entire argument completely ignores the fact that it doesn't matter if Youtube is offering 50Mbps streaming if the pipeline delivering the data is bottlenecking it at 5Mbps.

I try to give TB plenty of space for differing opinions, but he's just being a yutz on this one.

You can force youtube to give you a particular stream, even if your connection isn't the greatest and you're willing to wait for it to buffer. Detailed videos with high motion will still turn to garbage.

Waiting for it to buffer doesn't change anything. It's still streaming the data whether you're watching it as it streams or not. It's not downloading the original video file just because you wait for it to buffer. The only benefit to waiting for it to buffer is for extremely slow or unstable connections to avoid pauses during playback.
